text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Germany can no longer find understanding for 320,000 Bosnian refugees living within its borders because the country has been spending a great deal of money to support them, the international mediator for Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Christian Schwarz-Schiling tells news conference.
- Mayor of bitterly divided Mostar, Ivan Prskalo, warns the envoy of Bosnia's International High Representative in town, Sir Martin Garrod, of destabilisation in security situation.

- Bosnian Moslems and Croats agree to hold transitional municipal council session in town of Jajce March 15, but failed to agree on when to hold a similar session for Moslem controlled central Bosnian town of Bugojno, Schwarz-Schilling tells a news conference.
- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation Banking Agency issued 19 permanent permits for banks in Federation in 1996, agency manager Zlatko Bras tells a news conference.

- commissioner of the U.N. International Police Tusk Force (IPTF) Peter Fitzgerald was presented with shield and certificate of honour by Moslem-Croat Federation Interior Minister Mehmed Zilic after end of his mandate.

- Bosnian Serb Republic proposes two separate financial systems in Bosnia, thus preventing holding of the donors conference for Bosnia in Brussels. Condition for holding conference set by international community is single Central Bank for all of Bosnia.

- Yugoslav Minister of Foreign Affairs Milan Milutinovic asks Bosnian Ministry of Foreign Affairs to delay for a while opening of embassies in Belgrade and Sarajevo because of complicated situation in his country created by street demonstrations, daily cites diplomatic sources as saying.
- Session of Arbitration Tribunal for disputed Bosnian town Brcko will be held in Washington February 3-4, Moslem-Croat Federation arbiter for the town, Cazim Sadikovic, says in an interview.
